To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a newly identified alcohol oxidase gene in Yarrowia lipolytica mainly catalyzes the oxidation of ω-hydroxypalmitic acid to ω-pimelic acid.
the newly identified fatty alcohol dehydrogenese gene FAO1 is the main enzyme responsible for ω-hydroxylation in Y. lioplytica.
a novel fatty alcohol oxidase is responsible for the oxidation and thus for the accumulation of long-chain ω-fatty acids in Y.  lipolytica.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel approach for the biotechnological conversion of renewable resources.
the identification and deletion of genes involved in ω- and β-oxidation in Yarrowia lipolytica.
the identification of a novel alcohol oxidase gene, which is mainly responsible for ω-oxidation in Y. lipo lytica.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FAO1 plays the most important role in the ω-oxidation pathway of long chain fatty alcohols in Y. lipo lytica.
the alcohol oxidase is responsible for the oxidation to dicarboxyli acids and the alcohol dehydrogenas is responsible for the formation of ω-hydroxyl fatty acids.
the FAO1 is mainly responsible for ω-oxidation in Yarrowia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the deletion of FAO1 is the best way to increase ω-hydroxy acid formation, while the deletion of FADH is the best way for dicarboxy acid production.
the deletion of the alcohol oxidase (FAO1) in Y. lipo lytica is mainly responsible for ω-oxidation.
the FAO1 gene is mainly responsible in Y.  lipolytica for the oxidation of fatty acids to dicarboxyliac acids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FAO1 gene is a promising target for metabolic engineering of Y. lipolvtica to produce dicarboxyli acids.
